pages.text: The Akaishi Generator Matrix scales the standalone generator into a $(4)sealed-chamber multiblock$(0) that burns fuel at a fixed multiplier.$(br2)$(bold)Anatomy:$(0)$(li)Seal a $(4)closed box$(0) out of Generator Matrix Casings — the shell is an $(bold)odd-size hollow box$(0)$(li)Mount the $(bold)Matrix Controller$(0) in a wall$(li)Mount an $(bold)Energy Output Port$(0) and a $(bold)Fuel Input Port$(0)$(li)$(4)The inside must be completely empty$(0) — no internal parts needed$(br2)No sealed box, no work; break any casing and it shuts down instantly.$(br2)Two shell sizes follow: 3×3×3 (Basic) and 5×5×5 (Advanced). The controller block you mount decides the tier.

Your first step into scale: the $(4)Basic Generator Matrix$(0), a sealed 3×3×3 shell.$(br2)$(bold)Once formed:$(0)$(li)Output multiplier $(bold)×45$(0)$(li)Generation $(bold)3375 AE/tick$(0)$(li)Energy storage $(bold)5 million$(0)$(li)Fuel coefficient ×9/8: the same fuel yields about 1.13× more power$(br2)Don't forget an Energy Output Port in the wall — it carries a $(bold)100 million$(0) buffer that feeds your grid.$(br2)Building tips live in the "$(l:akaishi:matrix)Matrix Structures$(/l)" entry.

The endgame heavy hitter: the $(4)Advanced Generator Matrix$(0), a sealed 5×5×5 shell.$(br2)$(bold)Once formed:$(0)$(li)Output multiplier $(bold)×200$(0)$(li)Generation $(bold)15000 AE/tick$(0)$(li)Energy storage $(bold)50 million$(0)$(li)Fuel coefficient ×9/4: the same fuel yields about 2.25× more power$(br2)Both tiers share: the Fuel Input Port buffers $(4)27 stacks$(0) and feeds the controller on its own (item-pipe friendly); upgrade components push it further.$(br2)Still short on power? That's when the "$(l:akaishi:reactor)Reactor$(/l)" and the "$(l:akaishi:fusion)Fusion Reactor$(/l)" take over.

Suggested reading: master fuels in "$(l:akaishi:energy_basics)Akaishi Energy Basics$(/l)", then wire up the grid with "$(l:akaishi:energy_pipe)Energy Pipes$(/l)" and "$(l:akaishi:energy_cell)Energy Cells$(/l)"; the standalone "$(l:akaishi:generator)Energy Generator$(/l)" is the cheap alternative. General multiblock layout rules: "$(l:akaishi:matrix)Matrix Structures$(/l)".
